career_ladder.note: Combined Geo-Scientist cadres operate under the Geological Survey of India (GSI, Ministry of Mines) and Central Ground Water Board (CGWB, Ministry of Jal Shakti). Positions are recruited at both Group 'A' (Geologist/Chemist/Scientist B) and Group 'B' (Assistant Geologist/Chemist/Geophysicist) levels, following Central Scientific Services promotional cadres.

exam_scheme.note: UPSC conducts the Combined Geo-Scientist Examination in three stages: Stage I Preliminary Examination (Computer Based, Objective, two papers, 400 marks), Stage II Main Examination (Conventional, three discipline papers, 200 marks each = 600 marks), and Stage III Personality Test / Interview (200 marks). Marks obtained in all three stages are counted for final merit evaluation (Total = 1200 marks). In Stage I objective questions, one-third (0.33) marks penalty applies for each incorrect response.

financial_package.estimate_note: Calculated at Level 10 entry basic pay (₹56,100) for Group 'A' posts with 58% DA; Group 'B' entrants start at Level 8 (₹47,600 basic). Field duty postings in mineral exploration and hydrogeological surveying carry additional Daily Allowances and camp kit allowances.
official_perks: Government accommodation / House Rent Allowance (27%/18%/9% by city category)
Official transport or monthly transport allowance with applicable DA
Field exploration allowances, tentage/camp allowance during geological expeditions
Medical coverage under Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS)
Annual Leave Travel Concession (LTC) and defined NPS retirement benefits
